decisions.reason: Assigning mint #1 to a specific EVM wallet does not change the required Base network or network class.
This one-off direct transfer request does not revise which NFT state transfers during a secondary sale.
The destination for mint #1 does not alter the NFT asset type, unlimited supply model, price, or use of mint numbers as edition identifiers.
Transferring an existing mint to the founder does not change the secondary-sale royalty amount, enforcement mechanism, or marketplace policy.
The transfer destination for mint #1 neither changes nor resolves the existing uncertainty about state preservation during a future contract redeployment.
The ownership transfer does not change any required metadata field; mint #1 remains its own referral code under the existing metadata rule.
The requested post-mint transfer has no effect on ETH payment, swap, output-target, or shortfall behavior.
The message requests an operational transfer of one mint and does not request any change to product FAQ copy.
The designated ownership of mint #1 does not alter any About-page content.
The transfer changes a particular ownership record but does not change the existing rule that the dashboard must reflect actual successful NFT ownership.
Making the founder the holder of mint #1 does not change the Lit-based policy or mechanism for verifying NFT ownership before ebook access.

Ownership of affiliate code #1 changes the holder instance under the existing rule, but it does not change the commission amount, trigger, timing, payout mode, or rule that the associated holder receives the commission.
